chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him): From a man who was performing Tamattu' and forgot to shorten (his prayer) until he entered the state of Ihram for Hajj, he said:
"He seeks forgiveness of Allah, and there is no penalty upon him."

key_terms.أَحْرَمَ: Entered the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrim performing Tamattu', combining Umrah and Hajj
key_terms.وَلاَ شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: And there is no penalty/dam upon him
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten (the four-rak'ah prayer to two)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shorten their prayer during Umrah al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the omission of shortening prayers (Qasr) during the Umrah of Tamattu' is excused if done out of forgetfulness, requiring only Istighfar rather than a compensatory sacrifice (Damm). This ruling highlights the Shia principle of *'Illat* (legal cause) being absent in cases of unintentional error, distinguishing it from deliberate neglect. It underscores the ease (*Yusr*) in Hajj rituals, aligning with the Prophetic tradition that 'errors are forgiven for my Ummah.'
